## Why

ADR-146's date-correction work left two authority-bearing lies in the
release code: the S3 deferral was narrated as "2026-10-19 operator choice"
(a stamped chain date, never a clock reading — the true time lives only in
ADR-146's correction table), and the publish verifier hard-coded the
`p-17b713…` pins of a candidate the operator has already superseded (B-4 —
withdrawn from production-publication eligibility, retained byte-for-byte as
rehearsal evidence). And nothing stopped the next future-dated literal from
being typed into code, data, migrations or tests again.

## What this does

- **Release constants reference the recorded decision** (`ops/`).
  `EVAL_DEFERRAL_NOTE`, `EVAL_DISCLOSURE`, `DEFAULT_NOTE`, the module
  docstring, `journey_verify.py`'s deferral wordings and the CLI help/name
  text all drop `2026-10-19` and name the record instead: the GATE
  DECISIONS row "S3 human-evaluation spine — DEFERRED wholesale by the
  operator", recorded in commit `a33cd6ec`, with the true time kept only in
  ADR-146's appended correction table. `git grep '2026-10-19' -- ops/src`
  returns nothing; a regression test asserts the three notes carry **no ISO
  date literal**.
- **The superseded pin is parameterised** (`ops/release_publish_verify.py`,
  `ops/journey_verify.py`). The `PUBLICATION_ID`/`IDENTITY_DIGEST`/
  `FROZEN_SNAPSHOT_DIGEST`/`DESCRIPTOR_SHA256`/`RELEASE_MANIFEST_SHA256`/
  `EXPORT_MANIFEST_SHA256`/`RULESET_VERSION`/`DATA_RELEASE_ID`/`AS_OF_*`/
  `ARTIFACT_COUNT` constants and journey_verify's `CANDIDATE_*` constants are
  gone. A frozen `CandidatePins` dataclass is built by `pins_from_manifest()`
  from the packet's own `CANDIDATE_MANIFEST.json` — missing or empty pins
  fail closed (`PublishVerificationError`). `--candidate` is **required**
  (no production default). The gate readout stays the publish authority: it
  must name the manifest's publication, identity and frozen snapshot.
  `CORRECTION.md` § Supersession record naming the publication flips
  `PF.publish_authority` to `deferred` and the proof reports
  `subject.posture = "rehearsal evidence of a superseded candidate (B-4) —
  no publish authorised"` — owner P35.12, landing the true-dated candidate.
  The CLI prints the posture line. Tests derive expectations from the
  manifest, never re-spell the pin.
- **Whole-tree future-date literal test**
  (`tests/unit/test_no_future_date_literals.py`, in `make check` via
  `tests/`). Every tracked text file in `ops/`, `exports/`, `web/src/`,
  `connectors/` (incl. `data/`), `api/`, `db/` and `tests/` is swept: an ISO
  date/timestamp later than the HEAD commit time fails unless it sits in a
  B4 R5 real-world field (`valid_from`, `valid_to`, `expiry_date`,
  `end_date`, `effective_date`, `due_date`, `next_run`, `schedule_time`,
  `deadline`), carries `future-ok: <scheduled|real-world|synthetic|
  illustrative>: <reason>` or a `SYNTHETIC_` name, or matches an **unexpired**
  `allow` entry of `docs/build/tools/record_policy/history.policy` — the
  ONE allow-list, reused through `memory_guard`'s own `Policy.parse` /
  `r1_exempt` / `expired_allow` (an expired entry fails). `docs/build/
  planning/**` and `docs/build/logs/**` are never scanned. The failure
  message names file:line + the three fixes; the sweep prints a non-vacuous
  files/literals count. Fixture tests cover planted failure, real-world
  fields, both marker classes, `SYNTHETIC_` names, malformed markers, allow
  in/out of expiry, and past literals.
- **C-10 honoured byte-for-byte** (`db/sqitch.plan` L44–52). The nine lines
  are asserted byte-identical to
  `tests/unit/fixtures/sqitch_plan_L44-52_at_p34.22a_base.txt` (never edited,
  never re-stamped) and allow-listed by change id — name, dependencies and
  `planned_at` — through the existing expiring `allow db/sqitch.plan …`
  entries. Every line after L52 must carry a `planned_at` no later than its
  commit time; the ≥ 52-line assertion keeps the guard non-vacuous.
- **First-run findings closed honestly.** ~120 literals triaged: real-world
  contract/statutory dates and scheduled windows got inline `future-ok`
  markers on the literal's own line (or a real-world field name where that
  was the truth); JSON fixtures and multi-line shell strings that cannot
  carry comments got narrow expiring `allow` entries in the existing
  `history.policy` (each names its literal and expires just past it — the
  sqitch-fixture entries mirror the plan's own change-id entries; P34.22b's
  fixture regeneration is the named remover for the JSON captures).

- `sig-ops release-publish --candidate docs/build/reports/
  p32.23a-release-candidate` — `verdict=pass (26 checks: 25 pass, 1
  deferred)` and `posture: rehearsal evidence of a superseded candidate
  (B-4) — no publish authorised`; `live_verification=false` in the proof.
- `make ci-local` (the `SIG_REQUIRE_DB_TESTS=1` suite leg, Docker up) —
  ruff/format/mypy green; pytest **6547 passed, 2 skipped** (documented
  env-only skips; the GCP project-id leak check ran non-vacuously with
  `SIG_GCP_PROJECT` armed); `verify-gen` clean; `make test-db` —
  **498 passed**; `python3 docs/build/tools/memory_guard.py all
  --staged` — no violations.
- `db/sqitch.plan` — zero diff; base fixture byte-identical.

## What this does NOT do

No hand-typed event date remains in release code — but the recorded date
corrections of ADR-146 are append-only and untouched; `db/sqitch.plan`
L44–52 is byte-identical to base; no `ingestion_permitted` flipped, no
`HG-nn` ticked, no production mutation, no live/public/human claim
(`live_verification=false`); the release-identity decision stays with
P35.12; the fixture-capture-date and `sources.toml` corrections stay with
P34.22b.
